items.claim: In MarkupSafe 3.0.0, `strip()`, `lstrip()`, `rstrip()`, `removeprefix()`, `removesuffix()`, `partition()`, and `rpartition()` no longer escape their arguments.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The 3.0.0 changelog entry lists exactly those methods as no longer escaping their argument.

items.claim: The Sphinx configuration sets `project` to "MarkupSafe".
items.label: supported
items.reason: conf.py sets project = "MarkupSafe".

items.claim: The C extension uses PEP 489 multi-phase initialization as of version 3.0.3.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The 3.0.3 changelog records adopting multi-phase initialisation (PEP 489) for the C extension, matching the module slots in _speedups.c.

items.claim: `Markup.unescape` lazily imports Python's `html.unescape` and applies it to `str(self)`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `unescape` imports `html.unescape` inside the method body and returns `unescape(str(self))`.

items.claim: `escape(None)` converts None to the string `'None'`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The escape_silent docstring shows escape(None) == Markup('None') and the test asserts escape(None) == Markup(None).

items.claim: In `escape`, when an object has `__html__`, the method is called and its return value is wrapped in `Markup` with no escaping.
items.label: supported
items.reason: escape calls `s.__html__()` and wraps the result in `Markup` without escaping it.

items.claim: MarkupSafe version 3.0.0 added Python 3.13 and free-threading support while dropping Python 3.7 and 3.8.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Version 3.0.0 notes support for Python 3.13 and its free-threaded build and dropping 3.7/3.8.

items.claim: The publish workflow is triggered on push of tags and on workflow_dispatch.
items.label: contradicted
items.reason: The publish workflow only triggers on push of tags; there is no workflow_dispatch trigger.

items.claim: The tag pass in `striptags` finds `<`, finds the next `>` after it, splices them out, and repeats.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The loop finds `<`, then the next `>` after it, and splices out the range repeatedly.

items.claim: `Markup.__new__` on a plain `str` with `encoding=None` skips the decoding branch and passes the text to `str.__new__`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: A plain str lacks `__html__`, and with `encoding is None` the code returns `super().__new__(cls, object)` skipping the decode branch.

items.claim: The create-release job declares `contents: write` permission.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The create-release job sets permissions: contents: write.

items.claim: The tox `style` environment runs `pre-commit run --all-files`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The tox style env commands are [["pre-commit", "run", "--all-files"]].

items.claim: `docs/html.rst` states that because `__html__` bypasses escaping, the author must escape user-provided data inside it.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The doc explicitly says bypassing escaping means user-provided data such as a display name must still be escaped inside `__html__`.

items.claim: The `pre-commit` dependency group contains pre-commit and pre-commit-uv.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The pre-commit dependency group lists pre-commit and pre-commit-uv.

items.claim: The module-level `escape` function begins with an identity check `type(s) is str` rather than `isinstance(s, str)`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The fast path uses `if type(s) is str`, with a comment explaining why not isinstance/`__class__`.

items.claim: In uv.lock, sphinx-autobuild resolves to 2024.10.3 for Python < 3.11 and 2025.8.25 for Python >= 3.11.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: uv.lock is not included in the shown repository files, so resolved versions cannot be checked.

items.claim: The `_TPEscape` protocol is defined at lines 20-21 of `src/markupsafe/__init__.py`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: _TPEscape protocol is defined exactly at those lines.

items.claim: MarkupSafe 1.1.0 wrapped `__html__` results in `Markup` consistently.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The 1.1.0 entry states escape wraps __html__ result in Markup, consistent with documented behavior.

items.claim: `Markup("{0}").format(Markup("<bar/>"))` returns `Markup('<bar/>')`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: format_field returns value.__html__() for objects with __html__ (Markup returns itself), so the result is Markup('<bar/>'), as the analogous test asserts.

items.claim: `string.Formatter.vformat` assembles its output with plain string concatenation.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `string.Formatter.vformat` is standard-library code not contained in this repository.

items.claim: The `DO_ESCAPE` macro is defined at lines 18-72 of `src/markupsafe/_speedups.c`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The DO_ESCAPE macro begins on line 18 and its continuation ends on line 72.

items.claim: The three branch tests in `EscapeFormatter.format_field` are `hasattr` checks.
items.label: contradicted
items.reason: Only two of the three branches test with `hasattr` (`__html_format__`, `__html__`); the third is a bare `else` (with an inner `if format_spec:` test that is not a hasattr check).

items.claim: `Markup.escape` is a classmethod that forwards to the module-level `escape` function.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `escape` is declared with `@classmethod` and calls the module-level `escape(s)`, re-wrapping for subclasses.

items.claim: `Markup.__new__` checks whether the object has an `__html__` method and, if so, uses its return value.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `__new__` does `if hasattr(object, "__html__"): object = object.__html__()`.

items.claim: The project version in `pyproject.toml` is "3.1.0.dev".
items.label: supported
items.reason: version = "3.1.0.dev" in pyproject.toml.

items.claim: `Markup.format` delegates the work to `vformat`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `format` creates an EscapeFormatter and returns `formatter.vformat(self, args, kwargs)`.

items.claim: The `escape()` function escapes `"` to `"`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The native escape replaces '"' with '"', confirmed by tests.

items.claim: MarkupSafe 3.0.1 fixed compatibility with proxy objects.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The 3.0.1 changelog includes "Fix compatibility with proxy objects".

items.claim: The escape test suite includes a 2-byte Unicode test case `"こんにちは&><'\"こんばんは"`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: That exact 2-byte Unicode parametrized case is present.

items.claim: `Markup.format_map()` is defined at lines 317-323 of `src/markupsafe/__init__.py`.
items.label: contradicted
items.reason: format_map is defined at lines 327-333, not 317-323 (which contain partition/rpartition).

items.claim: `EscapeFormatter.format_field` with an empty spec calls `super().format_field(value, str(''))`, which returns the string unchanged.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The else branch calls `super().format_field(value, str(format_spec))`, which with an empty spec formats the value with `""`.

items.claim: `Markup.__mod__` escapes its arguments.
items.label: supported
items.reason: __mod__ wraps all interpolation values in _MarkupEscapeHelper with self.escape.

items.claim: MarkupSafe version 2.0.0 was released on 2021-05-11, added type annotations and dropped Python 2.7.
items.label: supported
items.reason: CHANGES.rst shows Version 2.0.0 released 2021-05-11, dropping Python 2.7 and adding type annotations.

items.claim: The Sphinx configuration sets `autodoc_member_order = "bysource"` and `autodoc_typehints = "description"`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Both settings appear exactly as claimed.

items.claim: `Markup.__html_format__` raises `ValueError("Unsupported format specification for Markup.")` for any non-empty format spec.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Non-empty `format_spec` raises exactly `ValueError("Unsupported format specification for Markup.")`.

items.claim: In `escape`, an object that is not exactly `str` falls through to the later branches instead of the fast path.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Only `type(s) is str` takes the fast path; otherwise execution continues to the `__html__` check and `str(s)` escape.

items.claim: The `escape()` function converts other types to string at line 45 of `src/markupsafe/__init__.py`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Line 45 is `return Markup(_escape_inner(str(s)))`, converting other types to string.

items.claim: An exception raised inside `__html__` propagates out of `escape`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: escape calls `s.__html__()` without catching exceptions, and a test asserts `ValueError` propagates.

items.claim: The tox `typing` environment runs `mypy`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The tox typing env's commands list contains ["mypy"].

items.claim: The `[tool.cibuildwheel]` section sets `build-frontend = "build[uv]"`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: [tool.cibuildwheel] sets build-frontend = "build[uv]".

items.claim: `Markup.__mod__` wraps each argument in a `_MarkupEscapeHelper`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `__mod__` wraps tuple items, a mapping, or a single value in `_MarkupEscapeHelper` before delegating to `str.__mod__`.

items.claim: MarkupSafe version 0.16 removed 2to3 and dropped Python 2.5 and 3.2 support while adding direct Python 3.x support.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Version 0.16 notes improved Python 3 support, removal of 2to3, and removal of Python 3.2 and 2.5 support.

items.claim: The `Markup` class defines `__slots__ = ()`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The class body contains `__slots__ = ()`.

items.claim: `Markup.__add__` returns `NotImplemented` when the operand is neither a `str` nor has `__html__`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `__add__` returns `NotImplemented` when the value is neither a str nor has `__html__`.

items.claim: If the object passed to `Markup()` has an `__html__()` method, the constructor calls it and uses the returned string.
items.label: supported
items.reason: __new__ calls object.__html__() when present and uses the result.

items.claim: `soft_str` converts a value to a string without flattening an existing `Markup` back to plain `str`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `soft_str` returns `s` unchanged when it is already a str (so Markup stays Markup), else `str(s)`.

items.claim: The pre-commit configuration includes the check-merge-conflict hook.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The pre-commit-hooks repo includes the check-merge-conflict hook.

items.claim: The C implementation in `_speedups.c` performs the same five replacements in one pass with the output sized ahead of time.
items.label: supported
items.reason: GET_DELTA sizes the output buffer in advance and DO_ESCAPE then performs the five replacements (", ', &, <, >) in a single escaping pass.

items.claim: The Sphinx configuration uses `get_version()` from `pallets_sphinx_themes`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: get_version is imported from pallets_sphinx_themes and used to set release/version.

items.claim: The `typing` dependency group contains mypy, pyright, and pytest.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The typing group lists mypy, pyright, and pytest.

items.claim: `escape_silent(None)` returns `Markup('')`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: escape_silent returns Markup() for None, which is the empty Markup string.

items.claim: At import time, markupsafe's `__init__.py` tries to import the compiled `_speedups._escape_inner` and falls back to the pure-Python `_native._escape_inner` if the C extension was never built.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The try/except ImportError imports _escape_inner from ._speedups, falling back to ._native.

items.claim: `Markup.__html__` returns `self`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: __html__ simply returns self.

items.claim: `Markup.partition` and `Markup.rpartition` pass their argument through untouched.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Both partition and rpartition call super() with the raw sep and only wrap the results, never escaping the argument.

items.claim: `Markup.split`, `Markup.rsplit` and `Markup.splitlines` wrap their results in `self.__class__`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: All three methods build lists of self.__class__(v) from the super() results.

items.claim: Objects implementing `__html__()` are not escaped by `escape()`; the method's return value is used as-is.
items.label: supported
items.reason: escape returns Markup(s.__html__()) without escaping the returned text.

items.claim: The last line of `Markup.striptags` is `return self.__class__(value).unescape()`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: striptags ends with `return self.__class__(value).unescape()`.

items.claim: `Markup.escape` compares `rv.__class__ is not cls` and, when false, returns `escape`'s result as-is rather than wrapping it in `cls(...)` again.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Markup.escape checks `if rv.__class__ is not cls: return cls(rv)` and otherwise returns rv unchanged.

items.claim: `Markup.__getitem__` wraps its result in `self.__class__`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: __getitem__ returns self.__class__(super().__getitem__(key)).

items.claim: `setup.py` checks that `platform.python_implementation()` is not in {"PyPy", "Jython", "GraalVM"} to determine `supports_speedups`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: supports_speedups is computed exactly with that set of implementations.

items.claim: The publish workflow artifacts are named `build-sdist` and `build-wheels-{os}`.
items.label: contradicted
items.reason: Artifacts are named "sdist" and "{platform}-{arch|all}", not "build-sdist"/"build-wheels-{os}".

items.claim: The tests workflow is triggered on pull_request and on push to main and stable branches, ignoring `docs/**` and `README.md`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The triggers and paths-ignore match the claim.

items.claim: When a marker is unterminated, the `striptags` loops `break` and leave the rest of the string unchanged.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Both while loops break when the closing marker (`-->` or `>`) is not found, leaving value unmodified by that loop.

items.claim: `in`, `find` and `index` on `Markup` never escape their argument.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Markup defines no __contains__, find, or index overrides, so those inherited str methods do not escape their arguments, as the changelog also notes.

items.claim: In `_speedups.c`, if the scan finds nothing to escape it increments the refcount and returns the same string object.
items.label: supported
items.reason: When delta is 0 the code does Py_INCREF(in) and returns the same object.

items.claim: `Markup.__add__` passes the operand through `self.escape(value)`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: __add__ calls super().__add__(self.escape(value)).

items.claim: The C implementation in `_speedups.c` writes each replacement directly to an output buffer in a single pass.
items.label: supported
items.reason: DO_ESCAPE walks the input once writing escape sequences and copied chunks directly into the preallocated output buffer.

items.claim: Both `striptags` passes use `str.find` rather than a regular expression.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Both the comment-removal and tag-removal loops use value.find(...) with no regex.

items.claim: `_native._escape_inner` replaces `&` with `&` first, then `>`, `<`, `'`, and `"`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The chained replaces are in exactly the order &, >, <, ', ".

items.claim: The coverage report `exclude_also` includes "if t.TYPE_CHECKING", "raise NotImplementedError", and an ellipsis pattern.
items.label: supported
items.reason: exclude_also lists those three patterns including the ellipsis regex.

items.claim: The module-level `escape` always constructs a plain `Markup`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Every return path of escape() constructs Markup(...) directly.

items.claim: `Markup.join()` is defined at lines 170-171 and escapes each element of the iterable before joining.
items.label: supported
items.reason: join is at those lines and maps self.escape over the iterable before joining.

items.claim: On tag push, the create-release job runs `gh release create --draft` with the dist files.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The create-release job runs gh release create --draft ... dist/* on tag pushes.

items.claim: `Markup.strip`, `lstrip` and `rstrip` pass their argument through without escaping.
items.label: supported
items.reason: lstrip, rstrip, and strip pass chars straight to super() without escaping.

items.claim: `Markup.__html_format__` returns `self` when the format spec is empty.
items.label: supported
items.reason: __html_format__ raises on a non-empty spec and otherwise returns self.

items.claim: `repr(Markup("test"))` returns `"Markup('test')"`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: __repr__ formats as class name plus str repr, yielding Markup('test').

items.claim: `Markup.__add__` calls `super().__add__(...)` and wraps the result in `self.__class__` rather than a hard-coded `Markup`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The result of super().__add__ is wrapped in self.__class__, not a literal Markup.

items.claim: `_native._escape_inner()` is defined at lines 1-8 of `src/markupsafe/_native.py`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The file defines _escape_inner spanning lines 1-8.

items.claim: `str.__new__` on the `Markup` subclass allocates a new object even when no replacement ran.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The repository only shows the super().__new__ call; whether CPython's str.__new__ allocates a fresh object for a subclass is behavior outside this code.

items.claim: The `[tool.gha-update]` section sets `tag-only = ["slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator"]`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: [tool.gha-update] has tag-only = ["slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator"].
